tau_s.source: prior from reviews; fit by hazard model on published retention

theta.source: prior; set to P90 of max D on target videos

wps.source: tone study: Fireship 3.5, Drinker 3.0-3.3 words/s inside phrases

laugh_floor_per_min.source: SEEN calibration on one approved and one rejected film: the approved film read 4.29 for the channel audience and 3.81 for its topic audience; the rejected film read 2.71 and 2.37. The floor stays at the Fireship P25 of calibration run 3 (2.99), which lies in the gap. There is no ceiling: the approved film's SEEN read is 4.29 and no rejected film was ever too funny.

min_fact_laugh_share.source: measurement review. The SEEN calibration pair does not separate on it: approved 0.333 / 0.314, rejected 0.286 / 0.286; the gap is one bit of the rejected film's 21 laughs and the approved film fails 0.5 itself. Advisory (G5f) until a sample separates it.

follow_seconds_share.source: measurement review; kept by the SEEN calibration: the approved film is 100% / 100% followed, with no lost run and no weak retell unit; the rejected film is 96% for the channel audience but 67% for its topic audience, with a lost run of 4 and 5 retell units under 0.6. G4 separates on the topic audience only.

cringe_veto_p.source: calibration: second-family juror on 144 labelled seed lines, AUC 0.979; at 0.4 recall 0.92, false alarms 2% on real jokes and 2% on flat (calibration/juror-seed.jsonl)

peak.source: calibration run 1: P95 of E[laugh+½smile] over all target units is 0.50; every Fireship video has a mid-40% unit at 0.44-0.62

end.source: calibration run 1: best reference ending (N2TmzjbmjGM) has mean net +0.16 over its last 20 s; all Fireship endings are -0.32 to +0.03; take five -0.27

fact_encodings.source: Cepeda 2006; psychology review. A film shorter than short_below_s needs short_min encodings, not min (ruling 2026-11-09)

callback_min_gap_frac.source: the callback gap scales with the film, min(callback_min_gap_s, this share of the runtime); every film of 200 s or longer is judged as before

advisory_gates.source: SEEN calibration: G4 and G5 are hard, fitted on SEEN reads; the juror's cringe veto is advisory on meme bits until its meme calibration is ruled on (it was fitted on lines with no memes); the fact-laugh share is advisory because the SEEN pair does not separate on it.

laugh_cut.source: calibration run 1: P(laugh)+0.5 P(smile) >= 0.2 gives best F1 0.65 (precision 0.68, recall 0.63) against human joke labels on 8 reference videos

cringe_source.v: juror where it read the bit, else the judge model
cringe_source.source: juror cringe AUC 0.979 on seed lines; a general-purpose judge model over-calls cringe (14/48 cringe rewrites as lands) and reads 0.3+ on bits the juror calls clean

juror_cringe_map.source: isotonic fit of juror cringe score to the cringe label on 144 seed lines; calibration/juror-cringe-map.json

laugh_floor_persona_kinds.source: the floor applies to an audience whose persona is the channel persona (front matter `kind: channel`): the floor comes from comparable channels' references read with the channel card; a topic persona has no on-topic reference to fit a floor from

entertainment.source: G12 at the SEEN stage: each threshold is the midpoint between the SEEN reads of one approved and one rejected film (n = 1 + 1). Landed laughs/min (bits with laugh + 0.5 smile >= laugh_cut): approved 7.04 / 6.85, rejected 5.18 / 5.18. Library memes/min: approved 1.86, rejected 1.48. Longest voice run without a laugh or smile: approved 14.3 s, rejected 17.6 s. Meme time shown full, cutout or ghost: approved 64%, rejected 50%. The whole-cut juror's keep-watching read does not separate the pair, so it is not a threshold.
